sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]

admission assessment. [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]

Adviser contact [Standing rule]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application; Funding consideration [Standing rule]
December 1 priority; rolling until March 15 subject to remaining places. Standing annual dates: explicit
2026/27 year and time zone not shown. [s2]
Reference receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
All required materials by published program deadline; no separate reference grace period. Official final records
due by first class day. [s1]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Unofficial English scores suffice for review; official scores by first day of entry term if admitted. GRE deadline
not separately specified. [s1]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Exact acceptance deadline not publicly established in reviewed program/admissions sources; check
funding/admission offer. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
Proof via US degree/in-progress degree, English-only-medium institution, or TOEFL/IELTS/PTE/DET.
Mathematics-specific test minima not established here. [s1]

UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Degree earned or in progress at a US institution is explicitly accepted as proof; UChicago therefore satisfies
this route (inference from stated rule). [s1]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not required; consideration of unsolicited scores is not further specified. [s1]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Recommended, not required. [s1]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
Program promises tuition scholarship, stipend and health insurance; annual mathematics cash amount not
published in reviewed pages. [s2]
Years of support [Conflict]
Central PhD FAQ says five guaranteed years; mathematics says support throughout program. Written offer
should resolve duration beyond five. [s2] [s3]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Program funding statement is not citizenship-limited; international eligibility for on-campus work is stated
centrally. Verify appointment terms. [s1] [s2]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Central funding FAQ requires full-time enrollment and availability for assigned duties. Workload, summer
conditions and residual fees need offer confirmation. [s3]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
Standard PhD support described as part of admission; separate scholarship questions/references not
established. [s2] [s3]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
PhD Network lists fellowships/assistantships; federal need-based aid unavailable to international students. [s1]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 100 for PhD. [s1]
Fee waiver [Unresolved]
No mathematics/College of Science waiver procedure verified after targeted search. Ask COS PhD admissions
before paying; other Northeastern colleges' waivers do not establish eligibility. [s1]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Alina Marian
Moduli of sheaves and bundles, Quot schemes, enumerative geometry. [s5] [s6] [s10]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2025 preprint · A short way of counting maps to hypersurfaces in Grassmannians
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Jonathan Mboyo Esole
Algebraic geometry and mathematical physics, including elliptic-fibration/F-theory geometry, Lie-group
embeddings, Dynkin indices and representation-theoretic structures. [s9] [q14]

Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2025 · The topological life of Dynkin indices: universal scaling and matter selection
Research-paper evidence. Publication year is as stated; an old paper is not proof of recent activity.
Representation theory
Pablo Boixeda Alvarez
Affine Springer fibers and small quantum groups. [s5] [s6] [s7]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 listed forthcoming · Affine Springer fibers and the affine matrix ball construction for rectangular type
nilpotents
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Iva Halacheva
Geometric/combinatorial representation theory, crystals, quantum groups and categorical braid actions. [s5]
[s6] [s8]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Moduli Theory of the r-Braid Arrangement
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Milen Yakimov
Quantum/cluster algebras, noncommutative algebra and Poisson geometry. [s5] [s6] [s11]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint · Maximal green sequences for quantum and Poisson CGL extensions
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Valerio Toledano Laredo
Quantum groups, monodromy and differential equations. [s5] [s6] [s12]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 revision/publication · An abelian formula for the quantum Weyl group action of the coroot lattice
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Gordana Todorov
Representations of finite-dimensional and Artin algebras, quivers, cluster categories, triangulated categories
and tau-tilting theory. [b15] [b15p]
Current faculty; accepting new doctoral students is not publicly confirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Balanced Notation for τ-Rigid Pairs
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Complex geometry
Jonathan Weitsman
Symplectic/geometric quantization and Calabi-Yau geometry; adjacent to core complex-AG interests. [s5] [s6]
[s13]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint · Hilbert Polynomials of Calabi Yau Hypersurfaces in Toric Varieties and Lattice Points in
Polytope Boundaries
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.

Representation theory / homological algebra
Alex Martsinkovsky
Homological algebra, stable module categories, additive functors and torsion phenomena; connections to
representation theory and commutative algebra. [b17] [b17p]
Current faculty; accepting new doctoral students is not publicly confirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 journal volume; online September 2024 · The finite presentation of the stable Hom functors, the Bass
torsion, and the cotorsion coradical
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
